text:
alex: Quick follow-up to the rollout metadata RFC — proposal for a lightweight 'lease_bridge' layer to deterministically map freeform aliases to canonical refs/leases in the control plane.

maria: sketch the fields? client vs server responsibilities?

alex: fields idea: canonical_ref (semver or content-hash), lease_hint (seconds), compat_bands (list). Server resolves alias->canonical_ref and issues an opaque lease_token. Clients can opt-in to present lease_token for affinity.

sam: backwards compat ok. Race concern: alias flips during canary. How to make client idempotent? Need resolver version.

alex: include resolver_epoch in mapping response and emit in telemetry. Client retries if epoch mismatch. ops-bot: note: keep header numeric to keep size small.

jin: example for compat_bands?

alex: code:
```
alias: staging
canonical_ref: model-v2.3.1
lease_hint: 1800
compat_bands:
  - ">=2.0.0 <3.0.0"
  - "~2.3"
```
Clients validate canonical_ref against bands.

leo: prefer structured bands (enum + range) instead of freeform semver strings so runtime doesn't parse semver text.

maria: migration: many manifests have alias chains. Flattening at write-time? ops-bot: ops-sanity says flatten at write is cheaper; record provenance.

alex: plan: normalize on write, add legacy_aliases list for provenance, keep original alias if needed.

sam: testing: I'll add unit tests for epoch bump behavior and an e2e for canary transition to avoid 503s.

jin: security: lease tokens sensitive. Opaque UUID or HMAC? ops prefers opaque for rotation.

leo: opaque UUID + server mapping + TTL and revocation API for quick rollbacks.

maria: console UX: surface alias->canonical drift alerts when changes > X in 24h.

alex: I'll draft RFC follow-up with proto sketches + migration runbook. tagging eng-releases for playbook.

ops-bot: reminder: create follow-up in #eng-releases when RFC posted. Thanks! :thumbsup:
